title: `style` and `object` check the stack of open elements, which misses insertion
body:
`style` and `object` elements ignore insertion while the parser still has them on the stack of open elements. But [insert a foreign element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#insert-a-foreign-element) inserts before it pushes, so that check never applies to insertion. A parser-inserted `style` runs [update a style block](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-a-style-block) on insertion, with no children yet, and `object` queues an extra (re)determine task. XML empty-element tags such as `<style/>` are never on the stack at all (#13265).

WebKit and Gecko instead give parser-created elements a flag that is cleared once their children are done. The standard already does this for media elements with [blocked-on-parser](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#blocked-on-parser). But that makes element behavior depend on whether the parser created it. Alternatively, the HTML parser could push before inserting (computing the insertion location first), and the XML parser could keep an empty-element tag's element on the stack while inserting it. That would make the existing checks work, but `style` and `object` would still need to know about the parser.

`rel=expect` has the same gap, but Blink matches the standard there, so it's probably separate, although pushing first would change it too.
